status.stopped_info: The regulation is stopped, and all regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off. The configuration can be changed. When the regulation starts, the appliances are turned on again one by one.
status.start_refused: The regulation cannot start before the configuration is complete.
status.safe_state_text: The power sensor {sensor} gives no valid measurement. All regulated appliances and EV chargers are turned off. The regulation starts again by itself when the sensor gives a valid value again.
status.penalty_text: The tariff average has been above the power limit. All regulated appliances and EV chargers are kept off until the overconsumption is recovered.
status.safe_state_back_text: The power sensor {sensor} gives a valid value again. The regulation starts again with everything off at the next decision.
status.no_chargers: No EV chargers in the group.
status.waiting_ends_at: Turns on at the decision at {time}
status.waiting_charger: Waiting: another EV charger in the group is charging
status.next_ampere_at: One more ampere at the decision at {time}
status.finishing_at: Finishing the charging that went on when the charging window ended, at {current} A
status.power_runs_out: The power runs out here. What is below waits for free power.

general.tariff_window_info: The tariff window is fixed at one hour.

power_sensor.label: Power sensor
power_sensor.helper: The sensor that measures the total power of the house, in W or kW.

regulation_window_s.label: Regulation window
regulation_window_s.helper: The period the regulation average is calculated over. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

power_limit_w.label: Power limit
power_limit_w.helper: The highest allowed tariff average. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

turn_on_margin_w.label: Turn-on margin
turn_on_margin_w.helper: How far below the power limit the regulation average must be before an appliance is turned on. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

wait_at_limit_s.label: Waiting time at the power limit
wait_at_limit_s.helper: How long an appliance waits before it is turned on when the regulation average is at the power limit. Shorter when the average is lower. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

penalty_threshold_w.label: Penalty threshold
penalty_threshold_w.helper: How much the tariff average may exceed the power limit before a penalty starts. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W.

appliance_repeat_increment_factor.label: Increment
appliance_repeat_increment_factor.helper: How much the waiting time grows each time, as a share of the waiting time at the power limit. Default × {default}.

appliance_repeat_increments.label: Number of increments
appliance_repeat_increments.helper: How many times the waiting time grows. {min}–{max}, default {default}.

charger_repeat_increment_factor.label: Increment
charger_repeat_increment_factor.helper: How much the waiting time grows each time, as a share of the waiting time at the power limit. Default × {default}.

charger_repeat_increments.label: Number of increments
charger_repeat_increments.helper: How many times the waiting time grows. {min}–{max}, default {default}.

command_repeat_interval_min.label: Command repeat interval
command_repeat_interval_min.helper: How long an appliance or EV charger may go without a command before its last command is sent again. {min}–{max} min, default {default} min.

action_timeout_s.label: Action timeout
action_timeout_s.helper: How long an action may take before it is stopped and counts as failed. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

power_sensor_timeout_s.label: Power sensor timeout
power_sensor_timeout_s.helper: How long the power sensor may go without reporting before it counts as invalid. A HAN reader usually reports every 10 seconds. {min}–{max} s, default {default} s.

advanced.wait_curve_info: How much of the waiting time at the power limit an appliance waits, by how much power is free: the power limit minus the regulation average. The appliance is turned on at the first decision after the waiting time, so the actual waiting time is rounded up to the regulation interval.
advanced.repeated_turn_on_info: When the regulation turns the same appliance, or one more ampere for an EV charger, on over and over again, because it has to be switched off again each time and nothing else is switched in between, the waiting time grows. The first two times, the waiting time follows the curve. After that, it is the waiting time at the power limit, and it grows by one increment each time until the number of increments is reached. For the first two, the table shows the waiting time at the pivot point.
advanced.command_repeat_info: An appliance can change state without Kraftvakt, for example when its circuit breaker trips and comes back, or because of a fault in the device. The regulation therefore sends the command for the state it has set again when an appliance or EV charger has not had a command for this long. Appliances and EV chargers excluded from the regulation are left alone.
advanced.timeouts_info: An action that does not finish holds back the commands after it, also those that turn appliances off. A power sensor that has stopped reporting can show an old value as if it were valid.

appliances.priority_sub: Top = highest priority, turned off last
appliances.empty: No appliances yet. Add the appliances Kraftvakt may turn off when the consumption is too high.

appliance.variants_info: A variant gives the appliance another place in the priority list while its expression is true. The top true expression applies. A new variant is put at the bottom of the priority list. The expression and the actions of a variant are set when you edit the variant. The power reserve applies to every variant.

entity_id.label: Entity
entity_id.helper: The name in Home Assistant becomes the name of the appliance. The entity is available as entity_id and entity (the state object) in templates and actions.

power_reserve_w.label: Power reserve (optional)
power_reserve_w.helper: Free power that must be available before the appliance is turned on. Use it for appliances that draw a lot as soon as they are turned on.

override_turn_on.label: Override the action to turn on
override_turn_on.helper: Off: the variant uses the appliance's action to turn on. On: the variant has its own, for example another HVAC mode.

override_turn_off.label: Override the action to turn off
override_turn_off.helper: Off: the variant uses the appliance's action to turn off. On: the variant has its own.

action.entity_runs: Runs {service} for the chosen entity with the current as value.
action.no_default: The entity type has no standard action, so the action must be custom.
action.choose_entity: Choose the entity to use the standard action.
action.choose_action_entity: Choose the entity to set the value of.

condition.entity_helper: True only when the entity is on. Unavailable counts as false.
condition.template_helper: True only when the template gives the boolean value true. Variables: entity_id, entity.
condition.not_boolean: The template gives {value}, which is not true or false, so it counts as false.

actively_charging.power_sensor_helper: Above 100 W, in W or kW, counts as charging. Unavailable counts as not charging.
actively_charging.entity_helper: On counts as charging. Off and unavailable count as not charging.
actively_charging.template_helper: Only the boolean value true counts as charging. Anything else, also an error, counts as not charging. Variables: entity_id, entity.
actively_charging.not_boolean: The template gives {value}, which is not true or false, so it counts as not charging.

charging.name: Name
charging.name_sub: Shown in the priority list and on the status page.
charging.one_at_a_time: One EV charger at a time
charging.one_at_a_time_sub: An EV charger that charges may continue until the car is full or disconnected. The others in the group wait.
charging.chargers_sub: Charging priority, highest at the top. Drag an EV charger to another group to move it.
charging.no_groups: No groups of EV chargers yet. Add a group, and then its EV chargers.
charging.delete_group_not_empty: Move or delete its EV chargers to delete the group.
charging.switches_info: For each EV charger Kraftvakt makes three switches that can also be used while the regulation runs: «‹charger› excluded from regulation», «‹charger› override charging window» and «‹charger› finish charging after charging window».
charging.finishes_after_window: finishes ongoing charging after the window

charger.minimum_first: The charging current is always set to the minimum before the EV charger is activated or deactivated.

device_id.label: Device
device_id.helper: The EV charger in Home Assistant. Its name becomes the name of the EV charger, every entity is chosen among its entities, and the empty fields are filled with the entities it most likely has.

entity_id.label: Entity for allowed charging
entity_id.helper: Normally the charger's switch for allowing charging. The entity is available as entity_id and entity in templates and actions.

max_current_a.label: Maximum charging current
max_current_a.helper: Whole amperes. The minimum cannot be above the maximum.

power_reserve_w.label: Power reserve
power_reserve_w.helper: The power the EV charger draws when charging starts at the minimum current. {min}–{max} W, default {default} W (about 6 A on three phases, 400 V).

car_connected.helper: The car counts as connected only when the value is true. Unavailable counts as not connected.

actively_charging.helper: How Kraftvakt sees that the car is charging. Without evidence that it is charging, for example an unavailable entity or a template that fails, it counts as not charging.

charging_window.label: Charging window (optional)
charging_window.helper: Can span midnight. Start and end cannot be the same. Without a charging window, the EV charger is always allowed to charge.

finish_after_window.label: Finish ongoing charging after the charging window
finish_after_window.helper: An EV charger that is charging when the charging window ends may go on until it stops charging. Once it has stopped, it is not turned on again before the charging window starts.
